title: Licenses, call signs and renewal
blurb: Which classes exist, how call sign groups work, when you may transmit, and how long a license lasts.

T1C01.why: The FCC issues **Technician, General and Amateur Extra**.
T1C01.trap: Novice, Technician Plus and Advanced are no longer issued.

T1C02.why: Vanity call signs are open to **any licensed amateur**.
T1C02.trap: No class or years-licensed minimum applies.

T1C03.why: International communications must be **incidental to amateur radio** or **personal remarks**. Business is out.

T1C04.why: If the FCC can't reach you, it can **revoke the station license or suspend the operator license**.

T1C05.why: Group D is **two letters, a digit, three letters**: KF1XXX.
T1C05.trap: W1XX and KA1X have fewer suffix letters.

T1C06.why: Your license covers operating on a **US-documented vessel** with the **master's permission**.
T1C06.trap: No special FCC authorization is needed, and it isn't emergency-only.

T1C07.why: You may request renewal up to **90 days** before expiration.

T1C09.why: After expiring, you get a **two-year grace period** to renew.

T1C10.why: You may transmit once the grant **appears in the FCC license database**.
T1C10.trap: A CSCE, an ARRL listing or the mailed license isn't what authorizes you.

T1C11.why: During the grace period you can renew but must **wait until it is renewed** to transmit.
T1C11.trap: Applying for renewal isn't enough; wait for the grant.
